Cross-entropy on the written token is a KL divergence against a teacher that puts all its probability
on that token. **C**, logit distillation, puts the rest back. On the same rows and text as B, the 2B's
20 likeliest tokens and one entry for everything else are stored at every answer token, and the loss
is the forward KL, KL(teacher ‖ student): a *soft target*.

::: {.column-margin}
[Hinton et al., 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531). Scoring B's text once with the 2B took 1.56
GPU-hours and 490 MB (ADR 0010).
:::

The teacher is usually sure. Its written token is its first choice at 99.55% of answer positions, and
its top 20 hold all but 0.039% of its probability on average. So C differs from B only where the
teacher hesitates, as it does over `days` above.

**Result.** C ties B on test-clean (**82.5%**, 4.7 GPU-hours). On tools it never saw (BFCL) it leads
B, 81.6% against 79.1%, but not after correcting for the number of claims tested.
